Signals laid out on the ground
En vuelo, señales en el suelo; en tierra, izadas en un mástil.
A white 'T' in the signals area means that aeroplanes and gliders take off and land:
Parallel with the shaft, towards the cross arm
Parallel with the cross arm, towards its right end
Parallel with the shaft, away from the cross arm
Perpendicular to the shaft, on grass only
Paralelo al palo, hacia el travesaño. ★ Señales.
A landing T is laid out with its cross arm at the EAST end. In which direction do you land?
A white disc at the head of the landing T, or a black ball on a mast, means that:
Landing and take-off directions do not necessarily coincide
Landing is prohibited until the disc is removed
Gliders are flying and tow-ropes may be dropped
Right-hand circuits are in force for all aircraft
Aterrizaje y despegue pueden ir en direcciones distintas.
At an aerodrome with a variable circuit, a rectangular RED flag on the signals mast means:
A rectangular GREEN flag flown from the signals mast means:
A white dumb-bell displayed in the signals area means that aeroplanes and gliders:
Must keep ground movements to hard surfaces
May land anywhere on the aerodrome
Must use the grass areas only
Must not take off until it is removed
A white dumb-bell with a black strip across each circular portion means:
Use the runway for take-off and landing; taxi anywhere
Ground movements confined to hard surfaces only
Light aircraft only, on the grass strip
Con franjas negras: despegue y aterrizaje en pista, rodar libre.
A red square panel with ONE yellow diagonal stripe means:
The manoeuvring area is poor: take special care when landing
Landing is prohibited and the aerodrome is unsafe
The runway is for emergency use only, without facilities
Glider flying and winch launches are in progress
Una diagonal = cuidado especial. Aspa = prohibido.
A red square panel with a yellow diagonal CROSS means:
The aerodrome is unsafe: landing prohibited
A white letter 'H' in the signals area means:
Helicopters must use a designated area only
A hospital helipad is near the aerodrome
Holding is in progress over the field
A double white cross in the signals area, or two red balls one above the other on a mast, means:
A yellow cross on the aerodrome marks:
Zona para soltar cables y pancartas.
Two or more white crosses along a runway or taxiway, at intervals of not more than 300 m, mean:
That section is unfit for aircraft movement
That section is the glider landing area
That section is for emergency use only
That section is closed at night only
Orange and white wedge-shaped markers placed not more than 45 m apart indicate:
Límite del aeródromo (cada 45 m). Las marcas cada 15 m limitan zonas pavimentadas no aptas.
Orange and white markers spaced not more than 15 m apart signify:
A part of paved runway, taxiway or apron unfit for movement
The aerodrome boundary, on unpaved areas
The beginning of the runway available for landing
An intermediate holding position on the taxiway
15 m = zona pavimentada no apta. 45 m = límite del aeródromo.
A dumb-bell with a red 'L' superimposed means:
Light aircraft may use a runway or the area marked by a white 'L'
Left-hand circuits are in force for light aircraft
Landing is prohibited for light aircraft at this aerodrome
Low flying is prohibited for light aircraft in the circuit
L roja sobre la pesa = avionetas en pista o en la zona de la L blanca.
A white cross displayed at each end of a runway indicates that:
Landing is dangerous; aerodrome used for storage
The runway is reserved for gliders today
The runway is for emergency use only
The runway is open, but without lighting
Aterrizar es peligroso; aeródromo de almacenamiento.
At a disused aerodrome, a white cross plus a single white bar at each end of the runway means:
The runway is fit for emergency use only
The aerodrome is used for storage
Cruz + barra = solo emergencias (sin mantenimiento, puede haber obstáculos).
Two vertical yellow bars on a red square in the signals area mean:
Landing areas usable but without normal safety facilities: emergency only
Right-hand circuits are in force; use the right-hand runway
Glider flying is in progress; keep clear of the gliding area
Ground movements are confined to paved or hard surfaces
A runway-holding position on a taxiway is normally marked by:
Two continuous and two broken yellow lines
Dos continuas y dos discontinuas, amarillas.
At a runway-holding position marking, the broken yellow lines are on:
Las discontinuas, del lado de la pista.
After landing you vacate the runway and meet the BROKEN yellow lines of a holding point first. You:
Must stop and request a clearance
Must wait for the stop bar to go off
Saliendo de la pista no necesitas autorización.
Alternately flashing yellow lights near a runway
Steady red lights across the taxiway
Green lights along the taxiway centreline
Blue lights along the taxiway edge
Stop bars are found at aerodromes certified for:
Red lights at 90° to the taxiway, facing oncoming traffic
Yellow flashing lights at the side of the taxiway
Luces rojas a 90°, mirando al tráfico.
You receive a take-off clearance but delay before lining up, and the stop bar comes on again. Why?
Stop bars are on a timing circuit
Van con temporizador: si tardas, se encienden. Nunca cruces una roja.
An area with a history or risk of runway incursions
A runway whose surface gets very hot in summer
The area where aircraft are de-iced before departure
The area used for engine run-ups before take-off
Zona con más riesgo de incursión. ★ Importante.
When is it good airmanship to review runway hotspots?
At the planning stage, with the taxi route
Only when ATC mentions them on the radio
After landing, when vacating the runway
During the take-off run, when looking outside
Al planificar, con la ruta de rodaje.
A 'sterile cockpit' means that during critical phases of flight:
Only tasks for the handling and safety of the aircraft
The cockpit is disinfected before every flight
Passengers may not speak, even to report a hazard
The radio is switched off to avoid distractions
Solo tareas de manejo y seguridad. Los pasajeros sí deben avisar si algo les preocupa.
Which is NOT a recommended practice to avoid runway incursions?
Completing checks while crossing a runway
Writing down the clearance limit and marking it on the taxi chart
Listening to the ATIS before taxiing
Stopping and asking ATC if in doubt
No hagas checks al acercarte o cruzar una pista.
Taxiing, you are unsure whether you have been cleared to cross a runway ahead. You should:
Cross quickly if no traffic is visible
A sign with yellow lettering on a black background, such as 'B', tells you:
The taxiway on which you are
Amarillo sobre negro = posición: dónde estás.
A black-on-yellow sign with an arrow, such as 'J →', is a:
A direction sign: designation and direction of a taxiway
A location sign: the taxiway you are on
A mandatory instruction sign: hold short
Negro sobre amarillo con flecha = dirección.
A red sign with white inscription '09-27' at a taxiway holding point means:
Hold short of runway 09-27 until cleared
Runway 09-27 is located to your left
Blanco sobre rojo = obligatorio: no pasar sin autorización.
Hold short of the ILS critical area
The ILS localiser is ahead on the left
Protege el área crítica del ILS.
A sign showing a white number '4' on a black background beside the runway indicates:
Runway remaining, in thousands of feet
Distancia de pista restante, en miles de pies.
A white circle with a horizontal bar on a red sign means:
Stop and wait for the stop bar
Where there is more than one runway-holding position on a taxiway, the one CLOSEST to the runway is marked with:
Pattern A: two solid and two broken lines
Patrón A: la última antes de la pista. El B (escalera) es el de CAT II/III, más lejos.
A single broken yellow line across a taxiway marks:
Signals, including aerodrome visual signals and markings
The carriage of dangerous goods by air
Las señales están en el apéndice 1 de SERA.
An area beyond the runway, free of obstacles, under airport control
A paved area beyond the runway, able to bear the aircraft for stopping
The area of runway before a displaced threshold, used for taxiing
The graded strip on both sides of the runway, outside the edge lights
Zona libre de obstáculos más allá de la pista. Se suma a la TODA.
Stopping an aircraft in the case of an interrupted take-off
Stopping an aircraft after a long landing
Despegue interrumpido. No es para aterrizajes.
A stopway must be capable of supporting aircraft of approximately:
The length of runway declared available and suitable for the ground run of an aeroplane LANDING is the:
Cuatro Vientos RWY 09: TORA 1500 m, TODA 1500 m, ASDA 1554 m, LDA 1500 m. How long is the stopway?
Cuatro Vientos RWY 09: TORA 1500 m, TODA 1500 m, ASDA 1554 m. How long is the clearway?
Zaragoza RWY 12L: TORA 3032 m, TODA 3722 m, ASDA 3332 m. The clearway is:
Zaragoza RWY 12L: TORA 3032 m, TODA 3722 m, ASDA 3332 m. The stopway is:
As a rule, a clearway should not be longer than:
★ Importante: el CWY normalmente no pasa de la mitad de la pista.
A runway has a TORA of 2000 m. What is the maximum TODA it can normally declare?
Clearway máximo = mitad de la TORA = 1000 m → TODA 3000 m.
Fuerteventura RWY 19: TORA 2406 m, ASDA 3406 m. The AIP remark says the last 1000 m are not usable for take-off. Which statement is correct?
The last 1000 m can be used to stop, not for the take-off run
The runway has a 1000 m clearway beyond the TORA
The landing distance available is only 1000 m
Cuentan para parar (ASDA) pero no para la carrera (TORA). Por eso hay que leer las observaciones del AIP.
Palma RWY 24L: TORA 2590 m, ASDA 3000 m, LDA 3000 m. For a landing on 24L you can use:
The take-off run available in both directions
The part of the runway BEHIND a displaced threshold may be used for:
Take-offs in either direction and landings from the opposite end
Landings in the same direction only, after the threshold
Taxiing only, never take-offs or landings
Nothing: it is closed to all movement
Despegues en ambos sentidos y aterrizajes desde el contrario.
When a threshold is RELOCATED because of works, which statement is correct?
It closes part of the runway and also shortens the opposite direction; NOTAM
It only affects landings in that direction; no NOTAM is needed
It needs no NOTAM, because it is marked on the runway
It lengthens the runway in the opposite direction; NOTAM
Cierra parte de la pista y acorta también el otro sentido. NOTAM.
A runway is 45 m wide. How many threshold stripes does it have?
A runway is 30 m wide. How many threshold stripes does it have?
You count 16 threshold stripes. The runway is:
A runway 18 m wide has how many threshold stripes?
White arrows on the centreline before a threshold indicate that the threshold is:
Permanently displaced; area before it fit for movement
Temporarily displaced; area before it closed
Before an area unfit for any movement
Before an area usable as a stopway only
White arrowheads (chevron-shaped) across the runway before the threshold, with the designator not moved, indicate a threshold:
Temporarily displaced, for 6 months or less
Before a stopway, not for take-off
Puntas de flecha = temporal (6 meses o menos).
White crosses on the runway before the threshold mean that the pre-threshold area is:
Yellow chevrons before the threshold mark a pre-threshold area:
Fit for use as a stopway only
Fit for take-off in both directions
A Runway End Safety Area (RESA) is:
An area that reduces damage in an undershoot, overshoot or excursion
The paved stopway used in a rejected take-off
The clearway beyond the runway, free of obstacles
The engine run-up area next to the holding point
RESA. ★ Pregunta clave. No tiene por qué coincidir con el stopway.
An EMAS (Engineered Materials Arresting System) is:
An emergency braking system of material that crushes and stops the aircraft
A paved stopway able to support aircraft of about 23 000 kg
An area beyond the runway free of obstacles, used for climb-out
A lighting system that marks the end of the runway at night
EMAS: el material que se rompe y para el avión. Lo que los apuntes llamaban RESA.
Where are an aerodrome's declared distances published?
In the aerodrome section of the AIP (AD 2.13)
In the NOTAMs only, updated every day
In the aircraft flight manual, performance section
On the ATIS only, before each departure
TODA and ASDA are never less than TORA
LDA is always equal to TORA
ASDA is always greater than TODA
TODA is always equal to ASDA
Se suman clearway o stopway a la TORA. La LDA puede ser menor.
Which of these areas must be able to bear the weight of the aircraft?
El stopway, porque se rueda sobre él. Sobre el clearway se vuela.
According to ICAO Annex 14, the minimum length of a RESA beyond the runway strip is:
The TODA must allow the aircraft to reach the 'screen height'. For a light aeroplane (Class B) this is:
Complemento ATPL: 50 ft en Clase B, 35 ft en reactores. Lo verás en Performance.
Which of these is the pilot's signal to a marshaller to INSERT the chocks?
Palms facing outwards, hands moved inwards to cross in front of the face
Pointing at the wheels with one hand
Both fists clenched above the head
Both arms waved slowly above the head
Calzos puestos: palmas hacia fuera y manos que se cruzan delante de la cara. Retirar calzos: manos cruzadas que se abren hacia fuera. Freno puesto: mano abierta que se cierra en puño.
At night, a glider must show:
Lights similar to a powered aircraft, or a single red light
A red port light and a green starboard light only
Planeador de noche: luces de aeronave a motor o una sola luz roja.
A VFR pilot flies at 4000 ft. The distance from cloud that must be kept is:
Clear of cloud and in sight of the surface
VFR por encima de 3000 ft AMSL y por debajo de FL100: 1500 m horizontal y 1000 ft vertical de las nubes (visibilidad 5 km).
A flight plan was filed for a flight in uncontrolled airspace. The departure will be delayed by more than 1 hour and the new off-blocks time is unknown. The pilot should:
Cancel the flight plan and file a new one when the new time is known
Do nothing: the flight plan remains valid
Delay the original flight plan by phone
File a second flight plan without cancelling the first
Retraso de más de 1 h en vuelo no controlado: se cancela el plan y se presenta otro cuando se conozca la nueva hora.
For a CONTROLLED flight, the flight plan must be amended (or cancelled and refiled) if the departure is delayed by more than:
Vuelo controlado: más de 30 min. Vuelo no controlado: más de 1 h.
A horizontal RED square panel with YELLOW diagonals in the signal area means:
Landing prohibited (the prohibition may be prolonged)
Special precautions while approaching to land
Cuadrado rojo con diagonales amarillas = aterrizaje prohibido. Con UNA diagonal = precauciones especiales.
A horizontal RED square panel with ONE yellow diagonal in the signal area means:
Special precautions are required while approaching to land or landing
Una diagonal = precauciones especiales para la aproximación o el aterrizaje (p. ej. mal estado del área de maniobras).
A horizontal WHITE dumb-bell in the signal area means that aircraft must:
Land, take off and taxi on runways and taxiways only
Take off only to the right
Mancuerna blanca horizontal: movimientos solo por pistas y calles de rodaje.
A white dumb-bell with a black bar across each circular portion, at right angles to the shaft, means:
Land and take off on runways only; other manoeuvres need not be confined to runways and taxiways
Con barras negras: aterrizar y despegar SOLO en pista, el resto de maniobras es libre.
A double WHITE cross displayed horizontally in the signal area means:
Cruz blanca doble = hay vuelo de planeadores.
The letter C in black on a yellow background in the signal area indicates:
The location of the air traffic services reporting office
La «C» negra sobre amarillo marca la oficina de notificación de los servicios de tránsito aéreo (ARO).
An aircraft in flight sees a STEADY RED light from the control tower. It means:
Give way to other aircraft and continue circling
Luz roja fija en vuelo: ceda el paso a otros aviones y siga en circuito.
An aircraft in flight sees RED FLASHES from the control tower. It means:
Destellos rojos en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrizar.
An aircraft in flight sees GREEN FLASHES from the control tower. It means:
Return for landing (to be followed by a steady green)
Land at this aerodrome and proceed to the apron
Destellos verdes en vuelo: regrese para aterrizar; la luz verde fija llegará en el momento oportuno.
An aircraft on the ground sees a FLASHING GREEN light from the control tower. It means:
En tierra: verde fijo = despegue autorizado; verde intermitente = rodaje autorizado.
An aircraft on the ground sees a FLASHING RED light from the control tower. It means:
Taxi clear of the landing area in use
En tierra: rojo fijo = pare; rojo intermitente = despeje el área de aterrizaje en uso.
When a search and rescue operation is initiated, responsibility for alerting individual appropriate search and rescue units rests with the:
El RCC (centro coordinador de salvamento) alerta y coordina a los medios SAR.
The length of unobstructed runway that will support the aircraft during take-off is the:
TORA: longitud de pista declarada disponible y adecuada para la carrera de despegue.
Which of the following light signals, used at night by the control tower, clears you to taxi on the manoeuvring area providing that you are satisfied that it is safe to do so?
En tierra: verde fija = autorizado a despegar; verde intermitente = autorizado a rodar. Roja fija = stop; roja intermitente = despeja la pista; blanca intermitente = vuelve al punto de partida.
A flashing green light from the tower to an aircraft on the ground means:
Verde intermitente en tierra: autorizado a rodar.
What is the definition of the combination of take-off run available and the stopway?
ASDA = TORA + stopway. TODA = TORA + clearway.
You are approaching an aerodrome with a view to landing. What does a red flashing light mean when beamed at your aircraft at night?
Do not land, airport is closed
Go around, do not land. (You may re-enter the circuit)
Landing is dangerous, proceed with caution
Roja intermitente en vuelo: aeródromo inseguro, no aterrices. Roja fija: cede y sigue en circuito.
The meaning of a flashing red light signal, sent from ATC to an aircraft on the ground is...
Move clear of the landing area
Return to the starting point on the aerodrome
Roja intermitente en tierra: despeja el área de aterrizaje. Roja fija: stop.
A runway’s Accelerate Stop Distance Available (ASDA) is defined as...
The TORA plus the length of the stopway
Always being the same as the LDA
Never being greater than the TORA
The TODA plus the length of the clearway
A red and yellow striped arrow, bent clockwise through 90 degrees and displayed in the signals square means:
Right-hand traffic required whilst on taxiways.
You should join at right base.
Flecha roja y amarilla doblada 90° en sentido horario: circuito a derechas.
Regarding taxi procedures and holding points:
The position of holding points ensures safe clearance between the aircraft holding and any aircraft passing in front or behind of the holding aircraft
You may cross a dashed yellow line only after checking left and right and if there is an ATC unit at the aerodrome, a specific clearance to do so
You may cross two solid and two broken yellow lines only after checking left and right and if there is an ATC unit at the aerodrome, a specific clearance to do so
You may cross red stop bars, if you have checked it is clear
Los puntos de espera protegen la pista; las barras de parada rojas no se cruzan nunca sin autorización.
090: Who may declare an emergency for any condition that they feel endangers the aircraft and its occupants?
Only a pilot holding a CPL
You declared a MAYDAY, and now the situation is under control and no longer time-critical. You may:
Cancel it only by phone after landing
Which situation is listed in the course as a PAN PAN (urgency)?
Which situation is listed in the course as a MAYDAY (distress)?
El temario pone el fallo de tren en MAYDAY.
Distress, as opposed to urgency, is a condition that:
Distress requiere asistencia inmediata; urgency no.
Once the situation is contained, the 'NITS' briefing to ATC stands for:
After transmitting a MAYDAY or PAN call, and unless instructed otherwise by ATC, set the transponder to:
A passenger becomes ill but the flight is otherwise normal. The correct prefix is:
You detect a fuel leak in flight. The correct prefix is:
Which is a time-critical event and therefore a MAYDAY?
Fuego o humo = MAYDAY. Las otras tres = PAN.
Your radio fails completely but everything else works. Squawk:
MAYDAY is used when the aircraft is:
Threatened by grave and/or imminent danger and requires immediate assistance
In a situation affecting safety that does not require immediate assistance
Short of fuel but able to reach the destination with reserves
An urgency that does not require immediate assistance
Grave and imminent danger requiring immediate assistance
A routine position report on a busy frequency
Unlawful interference on board the aircraft
